Practice Makes Perfect: Complete Japanese Grammar

is a comprehensive self-study workbook designed to build mastery of Japanese grammar through clear explanations, practical examples, and extensive exercises, authored by Eriko Sato and published by McGraw Hill.
It provides 200 exercises organized into 15 units that cover all major aspects of Japanese grammar, with explanations that incorporate helpful comparisons to English grammar structures.
Example sentences are presented in Japanese script (hiragana, katakana, and kanji) alongside romanization to support pronunciation and reading practice.
Eriko Sato, the author, brings extensive experience as an educator and curriculum developer in Japanese language instruction.

First published in 2014 with a Premium Second Edition released in 2021, it functions as a hands-on resource designed to build proficiency in reading, writing, and speaking Japanese through structured grammar practice.

The Term Perfectionism | Organizing a Common Term for the Tendency to Feel That One Must Be Perfect
You may have come across the term "perfectionism" in books or online. In this article, we will organize the general meaning of this term and points to keep in mind when using it.
■ What is perfectionism?

Perfectionism is a common term that generally describes a tendency to feel that one "must be perfect" or that "there must be no mistakes." While it is used in psychology and self-help contexts, it is not a diagnostic label. It is also not a term that determines whether a personality is good or bad.
■ Examples that are easy to imagine in daily life
・When finishing work or assignments: "It's still not enough," "I'm afraid of making mistakes."
・Before a submission or presentation: "I can't submit it unless it's perfect."
